title: Ramesh Traders v. CIT Chennai
text: The assessee, Ramesh Traders, challenges the assessment order under Section 143(3) of the Income Tax Act wherein the Commissioner of Income Tax added unexplained cash credits to the assessee's income. The assessee argued that the cash credits represented loans from friends and relatives and filed confirmations and affidavits. The Commissioner of Income Tax found the explanation unsatisfactory and made additions. The Income Tax Appellate Tribunal upheld the assessment order. The High Court examined the evidence. Mere filing of affidavits without documentary proof of creditworthiness of creditors is insufficient to discharge the burden of proof. The assessment order adding cash credits to income under Section 68 is upheld. The deduction claim under Section 80C for the tax year is allowed in part. The Commissioner of Income Tax's assessment order is confirmed with modifications.
